ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Patient consulted for 3-day history of diarrhea with abdominal pain and intermittent vomiting; no obvious food, drug, or environmental trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Onset 3 days ago; diarrhea persistent, neither improving nor worsening.
  • One episode of vomiting this morning after eating fruit; nausea resolved after vomiting.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied.
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: Denied.
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported.
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: Denied.
  • Dyspnea: Baseline mild asthma only; no acute worsening.
  • Swelling of lips/tongue/uvula/face: Denied.
  • Ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling: Denied.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No previous similar ENT swelling episodes.
  • No prior ED visits or epinephrine injections for allergy.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: “NKDA” (No Known Drug Allergies).
  • Asthma inhaler (brand unspecified)—dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Relevant social context:
  • Staying at home; not currently at work due to frequent need for toilet access.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported or observed (remote video).
- Airway/breathing: Speaking in full sentences; no audible wheeze or stridor reported.
- Mental status: Alert and oriented; converses appropriately.
- Vitals and physical exam: Not recorded.
- Accompaniment: Not specified.

Assessment:
- No evidence of acute ENT pathology (no airway compromise, no oropharyngeal or facial swelling).
- Presentation most consistent with gastroenteritis; baseline controlled asthma noted.

Plan:
- No ENT-specific intervention required at this time.
- General advice given (hydration, monitor for fever, seek in-person GP review if worsening).
- Red-flag advice emphasized:
  • If any throat tightness, voice change, difficulty breathing, facial/lip/tongue swelling, stridor, or inability to swallow/handle secretions develops, call emergency services (999) immediately.
- Follow-up:
  • Patient to arrange GP appointment if symptoms persist > 24–48 hrs or worsen.
  • Consider future allergy/immunology or ENT referral only if any new airway or swelling symptoms occur.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: Vitals, focused ENT physical examination (oropharyngeal visualization, neck exam), detailed asthma medication name/dose/frequency, availability of rescue inhaler or epinephrine auto-injector not discussed.
• Internal conflicts: None identified.
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional incomplete sentences but clinical content understandable.
